newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes at seven-month high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes at seven-month high.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at a seven-month high against the U.S. dollar on Thursday and dealers said the local unit was likely to remain strong.

The central bank's comments after Wednesday's close that recent market volatility was both normal and beneficial further helped the Taiwan dollar's upward trend, pushing the rate to T$27.270 at the opening, they said.

The local unit ended at T$27.338, the highest level since its T$27.312 close on May 21, 1996, and firmer than Wednesday's T$27.382 finish. Turnover through dealers fell to US$357 million from Wednesday's US$468 million.
"It's not clear what the central bank's limits are, though it said it would respect market forces, so investors turned cautious today," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said foreign equity fund inflows and traditional Taiwan dollar demand before the February 7 lunar new year likely would keep the local unit stable in the near term.
"It's not likely the Taiwan dollar will stand above T$27.30 though it did break that level this morning," said another dealer, noting the U.S. dollar's afternoon strength overseas.
A T$27.30-35 range was seen for Friday.
